synthesis.formal_statement: Entropy of an isolated system never decreases: ΔS ≥ 0. Defines arrow of time and irreversibility

ontological_structures.evidence: PRIMARY — law IS about temporal process: entropy growth, irreversible evolution, time's arrow
Distinguishes reversible (ΔS=0) from irreversible (ΔS>0) processes
Relates entropy to heat flow and temperature

synthesis.dimension_hints: D=4 (field/temporal) — defines temporal directionality, arrow of time
synthesis.elimination_test: Remove ⟳ (temporal directionality, irreversible growth) → law vanishes, it IS about time's arrow. Remove Δ (reversible/irreversible distinction) → consequence of entropy growth. Remove ⇄ (entropy-heat relation) → mechanism. ⟳ is essential.

synthesis.formal_statement: dU = δQ - δW — energy is conserved, internal energy changes via heat and work

ontological_structures.evidence: PRIMARY — law IS the relation: energy ↔ heat ↔ work, conservation via transformations
Heat and work are processes
Distinguishes different energy forms (internal, heat, work)

synthesis.elimination_test: Remove ⇄ (energy transformation relations) → law vanishes, it IS the conservation balance. Remove ⟳ (heat/work processes) → context but relation remains. Remove Δ → relation still holds. ⇄ is essential.

synthesis.formal_statement: S = k_B ln W — entropy relates macrostate to number of microstates

ontological_structures.evidence: PRIMARY — entropy IS the relation: macrostate ↔ microstate multiplicity
Distinguishes ordered (low S) from disordered (high S) states
Minimal — static measure, though entropy grows in processes

synthesis.elimination_test: Remove ⇄ (macro↔micro relation) → entropy vanishes, it IS the statistical link. Remove Δ (order/disorder) → consequence of measure. Remove ⟳ → measure itself is static. ⇄ is essential.

synthesis.formal_statement: Idealized reversible heat engine cycle defining maximum efficiency: η = 1 - T_c/T_h

ontological_structures.evidence: PRIMARY — Carnot IS a cyclic process: isothermal expansion → adiabatic → isothermal compression → adiabatic
Relates efficiency to temperature ratio
Distinguishes reversible limit from real irreversible engines

synthesis.dimension_hints: D=3 (volumetric) — operates on gas volume in cylinder
synthesis.elimination_test: Remove ⟳ (cyclic process) → Carnot vanishes, it IS the four-stage cycle. Remove ⇄ (efficiency relation) → consequence of cycle. Remove Δ (reversible limit) → idealization context. ⟳ is essential.

synthesis.formal_statement: G = H - TS — determines spontaneity at constant T,P: ΔG < 0 for spontaneous processes

ontological_structures.evidence: PRIMARY — Gibbs IS the relation: enthalpy ↔ entropy ↔ spontaneity criterion
Distinguishes spontaneous (ΔG<0) from non-spontaneous (ΔG>0)
Minimal — function determines process direction but is itself static

synthesis.dimension_hints: D=3 (volumetric) — applies to chemical systems at constant pressure
synthesis.elimination_test: Remove ⇄ (H-TS relation) → Gibbs vanishes, it IS the thermodynamic potential formula. Remove Δ (spontaneity criterion) → consequence of ΔG sign. Remove ⟳ → already static function. ⇄ is essential.

synthesis.formal_statement: f(v) ∝ v² exp(-mv²/2k_BT) — probability distribution of molecular velocities in ideal gas

ontological_structures.evidence: PRIMARY — distribution IS the relation: temperature ↔ velocity statistics
Distinguishes different temperature regimes
Molecular motion is continuous process, but distribution is static

synthesis.elimination_test: Remove ⇄ (T↔v relation) → distribution vanishes, it IS the statistical formula. Remove Δ → temperature distinction is consequence. Remove ⟳ (molecular motion) → context, distribution itself static. ⇄ is essential.

synthesis.formal_statement: Impossible to construct device that transfers heat from cold to hot reservoir without external work

ontological_structures.evidence: PRIMARY — principle IS the impossibility distinction: what engines can vs cannot do
Heat flow and work are temporal processes
Relates heat reservoirs via temperature gradient

synthesis.dimension_hints: D=3 (volumetric) — heat engines operate on working substance in 3D
synthesis.elimination_test: Remove Δ (impossibility statement) → principle vanishes, it IS about the forbidden operation. Remove ⟳ (heat flow process) → context for impossibility. Remove ⇄ → heat gradient presupposed. Δ is essential.

synthesis.formal_statement: Reversible: quasistatic, no entropy generation (ΔS=0). Irreversible: real processes with entropy increase (ΔS>0)

ontological_structures.evidence: PRIMARY — concept IS the distinction: reversible (ideal, no dissipation) vs irreversible (real, entropy-generating)
Both types describe temporal processes
Relates entropy change to process type

synthesis.dimension_hints: D=4 (field/temporal) — temporal asymmetry, arrow of time
synthesis.elimination_test: Remove Δ (the classification itself) → distinction vanishes, it IS about categorizing processes. Remove ⟳ (temporal evolution) → context for classification. Remove ⇄ (entropy relation) → consequence. Δ is essential.

synthesis.formal_statement: When system at equilibrium is disturbed, it shifts to counteract the disturbance and restore equilibrium

ontological_structures.evidence: PRIMARY — principle IS about dynamic response: perturbation → shift → new equilibrium (temporal evolution)
Relates perturbation to system response
Distinguishes equilibrium states before and after perturbation

synthesis.dimension_hints: D=3 (volumetric) — applies to chemical systems in reactors
synthesis.elimination_test: Remove ⟳ (dynamic equilibrium shift) → principle vanishes, it IS about the temporal response process. Remove ⇄ (perturbation↔response relation) → important but process is essence. Remove Δ → equilibrium states are context. ⟳ is essential.

synthesis.formal_statement: If A in thermal equilibrium with B, and B with C, then A in equilibrium with C — defines temperature transitivity

ontological_structures.evidence: PRIMARY — law IS the transitive relation: A↔B, B↔C ⇒ A↔C (thermal equilibrium)
Distinguishes thermal equilibrium from non-equilibrium
Minimal — law about equilibrium (static), not approach to equilibrium

synthesis.elimination_test: Remove ⇄ (transitivity relation) → law vanishes, it IS the transitive property. Remove Δ (equilibrium distinction) → presupposed by relation. Remove ⟳ → already about static equilibrium. ⇄ is essential.
